activities.title: Library Read-Aloud and Word Hunt
activities.instructions: Visit a local library storytime or explore the early readers section together. Choose a story with some unfamiliar words. As you read together, encourage sounding out new or tricky words syllable by syllable using phonetic clues, offering gentle guidance and celebrating successful attempts.

activities.title: Two-Digit Strategy Showcase
activities.instructions: Write out a few two-digit addition or subtraction problems on paper cards (such as 34 + 25 or 58 - 23). Invite your child to solve each one using a familiar method (like splitting by tens and ones), and then challenge them to try a second strategy (like drawing an open number line or counting on) to show how different approaches reach the same solution.

activities.title: Balance and Movement Circuit
activities.instructions: Participate in a structured movement session focusing on gross motor coordination. Guide your child through sequential activities such as traversing low balance beams, jumping between markers, and controlled landing drills, focusing on smooth body alignment and steady balance throughout the routine.

activities.title: Step-by-Step Mini Craft Collage
activities.instructions: Design a small, structured craft project such as a paper plate mask or bookmark collage. Break the project into two distinct, quick stages (first stage: cut and paste base shapes for 5 minutes; second stage: add colour and details for 5 minutes), providing clear milestones so your child experiences the satisfaction of seeing a project through to the finish line.

activities.title: Nature Park Balance and Agility Adventure
activities.instructions: Visit a local park and set up a playful, structured movement sequence using natural and park elements. Guide your child to walk heel-to-toe along a low log or curb, hop on one foot across three designated grass spots, and hold a balance pose on a low flat rock or step for five seconds. Repeat the circuit a few times together to build confidence and body control.

activities.title: Bite-Sized Nature Texture Rubbings
activities.instructions: Step outside into the yard or garden to collect 3 or 4 textured leaves and small pieces of flat bark. Place one item at a time under a small postcard-sized sheet of paper, and show your child how to rub the side of a crayon over it to reveal the pattern. Keeping the canvas small provides a clear, reachable goal so they can see their finished art piece from start to completion in a single session.

activities.title: Library Sound-Out Story Hunt
activities.instructions: Visit a nearby children's library and select two short early-reader books together. Settle into a quiet reading area and invite your child to read aloud with you. When encountering an unfamiliar word, encourage them to identify each letter sound individually and slide their finger along underneath as they blend the sounds together, offering warm praise for their efforts.

activities.title: Society Pool Kicking & Stroke Adventures
activities.instructions: Head to your society's pool for fun, sustained water play. Practice kicking with a kickboard from one side of the shallow end to the other, pretending to be speedboats, and practice arm strokes with steady breathing breaks to build swimming stamina.

activities.title: Library Story Corner Word Decoding
activities.instructions: Visit the children's section to choose an engaging early-reader picture book. Sit together and take turns reading aloud, encouraging sounding out unfamiliar words phoneme by phoneme and blending them smoothly to build reading confidence.

activities.title: Community Art & Craft Exploration

activities.title: Robot Talk Decoding
activities.instructions: During shared reading time, pause together whenever you come across an unfamiliar or longer word. Take turns switching into a playful 'robot voice' to sound out each phoneme cleanly (e.g., 's-p-oo-n'), tapping fingers for each distinct sound. After breaking it down, blend the sounds back together in your regular voice to read the whole word smoothly, offering plenty of encouragement for trying new words.

activities.title: Living Room Balance Routine
activities.instructions: Create a clear, structured movement path on the floor using painter's tape or a line of cushions. Lead your child through a sequence: first, walk heel-to-toe along the line without stepping off; second, hold a one-legged 'stork' balance for a slow five count; third, make three slow, controlled two-footed hops forward, focusing on sticking a steady landing each time. Repeat the routine together several times to familiar music.
